lines.text: The first concrete lift sets out two walls. The space between them will become the cooling store.
Beside the pour, welders assemble the steel cage a level at a time. Building it here keeps the bore open while the walls rise.
The crane stacks each completed level on the last. Eight levels will carry sixty-four pods around a single central shaft.
Two crawlers lift the assembled cage and lower it into the bore. Watch the outer ring clear the concrete.
The bare support rig lands first. Its sliding collar braces the shaft before the first pod arrives.
Two pods arrive per truck. The gantry lifts one onto the rail, leaving the other receiving lane free for the next delivery.
Inside the bore, a pod rises and rotates into its berth. Its wall-end connections bring the cooling circuit online.
Outside, the crane hangs the cooler frames on cast-in wall seats.
The propane vessels arrive on separate transporters. They will fuel the turbines that supply normal operating power.
The tinted surface traces the liner up both walls of the cooling store.
On the laydown pad, crews prepare the power decks and stage the machines for the lift.
Four diesel sets land on the lower rig. They are reserved for emergencies. Water deliveries begin filling the store.
The two gas turbine sets occupy their own deck above the diesels.
The removable lid carries the air inlets and exhaust stacks.
Fuel lines run from the tanks, beneath the road and up to the machines.
One receiving lane becomes a glazed control room. The other stays open for pod exchanges.
At the centre, twenty-four anchors hold the steel shaft at its base. Four arms locate the collar above. The shaft can still slide vertically.
One four S U pod carries four racks between two trusses. At the wall end, the coolant distribution unit and pump travel with the pod.
Each frame holds three dry coolers. Here one coil and its pump pull clear. The fan bank discharges outward, away from the silo.
Lift the acoustic covers and the two generator sets come into view. Four rail girders carry their loads to the open ring and the wall seats.
At handover, two turbines supply the site. The operator can distribute up to forty-six megawatts of computing load across the installed racks.
On the silo roof, the red line marks the Starlink antenna's satellite link.
In plan, the pods draw cool liquid from the bottom of the store and return it warm at the top.
The dry coolers take heat from the top layer and return cooled liquid below. The section follows both circuits through the silo.
